literal: Virtue, wealth, pleasure, life-fear: of the four, the nature having examined, [one] will be trusted.
translation: A person should be trusted only after examining their true nature against four tests: virtue, wealth, pleasure, and fear for their life.
modern: அறம், பொருள், இன்பம், உயிருக்கு ஆபத்து வரும்போது ஏற்படும் அச்சம் ஆகிய நான்கு நிலைகளிலும் ஒருவனது இயல்பை ஆராய்ந்த பிறகே அவனைத் தேர்ந்தெடுக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the four fundamental tests for evaluating a person's character before trusting them with responsibility. The tests are based on how they react to the demands of virtue, the lure of wealth, the temptation of pleasure, and the fear of losing their life. By examining their true nature (திறம்) under these four pressures, a leader can confidently choose the right person. The compound 'உயிரச்சம்' (fear for life) specifically highlights the ultimate test of loyalty and courage when facing mortal danger.
